task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req173-wasm-module-hot-reload.md or similar) for REQ-173: WASM-14 hot reload. When a new version of a registered module is activated, in-flight invocations of the prior version must complete normally against the OLD version's behaviour and capability set; new invocations after activation must use the NEW version and its capability set. Design must specify: (1) how ModuleRegistry (REQ-166) is extended to support multiple versions of the same module (versioned registration, an activation operation that designates the current version for NEW invocations without affecting invocations already in flight); (2) the exact mechanism by which an in-flight invocation resolves and HOLDS its module version at invocation start, immune to a concurrent activation -- must be concrete and implementable, not hand-waved (e.g. does invocation start capture a version-specific struct/reference that activation cannot mutate out from under it?); (3) reference counting or an equivalent mechanism so the prior version's resources (compiled module, capability table, any other per-version state) are released only after its LAST in-flight invocation completes, never at activation time; (4) how CapabilityGate's per-manifest capability set is captured per-version so an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set even if the new version's manifest declares a different one -- this is a SECURITY-REVIEWER hard-gate concern (version confusion = authorization hazard); (5) the test design's own concurrency shape: the acceptance test must hold an invocation open (a guest blocked in a controllable host call -- consider whether an existing REQ-172/171 host function or fixture, e.g. one of the write_then_hang-style .wat fixtures, can be reused or adapted) then activate a new version DURING that hold, and assert both halves (old-version completion + new-version-for-new-invocations) in ONE overlapping scenario, with the two versions observably different in output. Explicitly out of scope: instance pooling (REQ-174 owns that interaction). Design only -- no implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: a test holds an invocation open (a guest blocked in a controllable host call), activates a new module version DURING it, and asserts the held invocation completes normally against the OLD version's observable behaviour -- WASM-14's own acceptance criterion, with the overlap real rather than sequential
the same test asserts an invocation started AFTER the activation observes the NEW version's behaviour, so both halves of WASM-14 are proven in one overlapping scenario
the two module versions used are observably different in output, so the test can distinguish which version served an invocation rather than merely completing
a test asserts the prior version's resources are released only after its last in-flight invocation completes, not at activation time

a test asserts that when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set, an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set, and the new invocation gets the new one -- so activation cannot silently widen or narrow a running invocation's authority
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
